name: Arabana-Wangkanguru
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand sources agree (1 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts
catalog_quote: Arabana-Wangkangurru follows the majority of Australian languages in having a strong stress accent on the first syllable of a word. There are no monosyllabics (except for Eastern Wangkangurru ko 'yes'); in words of two or three syllables there is simply the one accent falling on the first syllable.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, initial primary stress; secondary on 3rd/5th/7th with a morpheme-initial override in polymorphemic words) rests on the language's standard reference grammar (Hercus 1994, PL C-128, 324 pp.), which we hold in full; the deciding quotation was confirmed verbatim on printed p.47 (§2.12) from the page image, with the secondary-stress and morphological rule on p.48. Only defect: the long sources[0] cite gives 'pp. 48-49' where the printed pages are 47-48 (the domain locator's '47' is right) — a cosmetic locator fix, not a reclassify. Glottolog offers nothing better; a web search found no instrumental stress study of Arabana, and the one recent phonological analysis touching metrics (Harvey et al. 2019, downloaded, open) confirms initial primary stress and trochaic left-aligned footing citing Hercus 1994:47. No works still to obtain are warranted.
